Metadata.title: Emily Giuliana Scher | Frontend Developer
Metadata.description: Portfolio of Emily Giuliana Scher, a frontend developer specialized in React and TypeScript. Projects, experience and contact.

Hero.role: Frontend developer. I turn Figma designs into accessible, reusable React and TypeScript components.
Hero.location: Corrientes, Argentina. Fluent English. Open to remote work.
Hero.photoAlt: Portrait of Emily Giuliana Scher smiling

Projects.title: Projects
Projects.intro: One product of my own and two sites for local businesses in Corrientes.

stocknow.name: StockNow
stocknow.summary: Inventory and point-of-sale app for small businesses, designed for food venues, with an optional online catalog. The link goes to the public StockNow page.
stocknow.problem: Keeping track of a shop’s stock and charging customers quickly: products are loaded with their stock and description, combos can be set up, sales are charged from the cart and a receipt is generated.
stocknow.role: Co-founder and frontend developer. Modular architecture in Next.js, interface built with Tailwind CSS, data with Supabase (PostgreSQL and Auth) and views that depend on each user’s role (RBAC).
stocknow.imageAlt: StockNow page with a phone showing the product list with stock and prices

bonaBudin.name: Bona Budín
bonaBudin.summary: Online shop for a handmade loaf cake brand from Corrientes. Customers build an order in a cart and send it through WhatsApp.
bonaBudin.problem: Choosing size and quantity from a phone and closing the order on the channel customers already use: WhatsApp.
bonaBudin.role: I built the frontend: catalog, cart and sending the order through WhatsApp. The backend runs on Google AppSheet, where the products are managed.
bonaBudin.imageAlt: Bona Budín catalog with loaf cakes, their sizes and prices, and an add-to-cart button

carpinteria.name: Carpintería San José
carpinteria.summary: Online catalog for a woodworking shop in Corrientes, with products by category and direct contact through WhatsApp.
carpinteria.problem: Showing the shop’s products in a place of its own and making it easy for customers to ask through WhatsApp.
carpinteria.role: I built the frontend, in a repository of my own: products by category, search and contact through WhatsApp. The backend runs on Google AppSheet, where the products are managed.
carpinteria.imageAlt: Carpintería San José home page with the headline Handmade wooden furniture, made to measure, and a wooden desk

stocknow.b1: I lead the frontend with Next.js 15 (App Router) and React, organized into modular components.
stocknow.b2: I designed and built a responsive interface with Tailwind CSS.
stocknow.b3: I consume data from Supabase (PostgreSQL and Auth) and manage global state with Context API, rendering the interface according to each role’s permissions (RBAC).

makingSense.b1: I built accessible, reusable components in React and TypeScript from Figma designs, for a veterinary services platform.
makingSense.b2: I maintained the design system and led its Storybook documentation, working in an agile process tracked in Jira.
makingSense.b3: I implemented a strict component architecture and updated the previous component library.

freelance.b1: I built online shops and catalogs with shopping carts.
freelance.b2: I developed digital invitations as single-page apps, with forms, RSVP and date scheduling.
freelance.b3: I handed over documented projects so that each client could manage them on their own.

About.title: About me
About.p1: I’m Emily, a frontend developer based in Corrientes, Argentina. I turn Figma designs into accessible, reusable interfaces with React and TypeScript, working closely with design teams.

CaseStudy.metaTitle: Making Sense design system | Emily Giuliana Scher
CaseStudy.title: Making Sense design system
CaseStudy.lead: A library of accessible, reusable components for a veterinary services platform, documented in Storybook.
CaseStudy.context: Making Sense is a company based in Mar del Plata. Between February and July 2025 I worked with their team remotely, from Corrientes, on a veterinary services platform.
CaseStudy.role: UX / Frontend Developer, working in an agile process with tasks tracked in Jira.
CaseStudy.d1: I built accessible, reusable components in React and TypeScript from the Figma designs.
CaseStudy.d2: I maintained the design system in Storybook.
CaseStudy.d3: I led the Storybook documentation, meant to make onboarding new developers and maintenance easier.
CaseStudy.d4: I implemented a strict component architecture.
CaseStudy.d5: I updated the previous component library to the new system.
CaseStudy.note: I can’t show the code or the product’s screens. If you’d like to know more about this work, get in touch.
